text:
Predicates:
SuperheroMovie(x) ::: x is a superhero movie.
GoodGuy(x) ::: x is a good guy.
BadGuy(x) ::: x is a bad guy.
Fight(x, y) ::: x fights y.
Nemesis(x, y) ::: y is the nemesis of x.
NamedAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
AppearsIn(x, y) ::: x appears in y.
Wins(x, y) ::: x wins against y.
Loses(x, y) ::: x loses against y.
Premises:
∀x (SuperheroMovie(x) → ∀y (GoodGuy(y) → Wins(y, x))) ::: In superhero movies, the good guys always win.
SuperheroMovie(sirDigbyMovie) ∧ NamedAfter(sirDigbyMovie, sirDigby) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie. The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is named after Sir Digby.
∀x ∀y (GoodGuy(x) ∧ BadGuy(y) → Fight(x, y)) ∧ ∀x ∀y (BadGuy(x) ∧ GoodGuy(y) → Fight(x, y)) ::: Good guys fight bad guys and vice versa.
Nemesis(sirDigby, nemesis) ∧ Fight(sirDigby, nemesis) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
∀x ∀y (SuperheroMovie(x) ∧ NamedAfter(x, y) → GoodGuy(y)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is a good guy.
∀x ∀y (SuperheroMovie(x) ∧ NamedAfter(x, y) → AppearsIn(y, x)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character appears in the movie.
∀x ∀y (Wins(x, y) → Loses(y, x)) ::: If somebody wins a fight, the person they are fighting loses.
Conclusion:
Loses(nemesis, sirDigby) ::: Sir Digby’s nemesis loses.
